click_select.location: Results → Map window → Options panel: switch segment making a click select the feature's grid row

open.location: Results → Map window → Options panel: label of the switch opening the map automatically when the query finishes

open_auto.location: Results → Map window → Options panel: switch segment opening the map after every run

open_manual.location: Results → Map window → Options panel: switch segment opening the map only from Show on Map

limit.location: Results → Map window → Options panel: label of the dropdown choosing the feature cap

start_view.location: Results → Map window → Options panel: label of the switch choosing how the map first frames the data

view_fit.location: Results → Map window → Options panel: switch segment framing every feature when the map opens

view_current.location: Results → Map window → Options panel: switch segment remembering the current center and zoom

copy_directive.location: Results → Map window → Options panel: button copying the -- sqlly map: line to the clipboard

write_to_query.location: Results → Map window → Options panel: button writing the settings into the query's lock block

approval_approved.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Approval column: cell value for an AI-proposed write statement that the user approved in SQLLY but which has not yet finished running.

approval_executed.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Approval column: cell value for an AI-proposed write statement that was approved and then actually run against the database.

approval_expired.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Approval column: cell value for an AI-proposed write statement that nobody approved or rejected before it timed out.

approval_pending.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Approval column: cell value for an AI-proposed write statement still waiting for the user to approve or reject it in SQLLY.

approval_rejected.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Approval column: cell value for an AI-proposed write statement that the user declined, so it was never run.

browser_unavailable.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Error line: feature name inserted into the “not available in the browser preview” message shown instead of the activity log when SQLLY runs in a web browser; a short noun phrase.

column_approval.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Activity grid: column header for the approval state of AI-proposed write statements (pending, approved, rejected, expired, executed); blank for read-only tool calls.

column_connection.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Activity grid: column header for the name of the saved connection an MCP tool call ran against.

column_database.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Activity grid: column header for the database name an MCP tool call targeted on that connection.

column_duration.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Activity grid: column header for how long each MCP tool call took, in milliseconds; keep the unit abbreviation.

column_outcome.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Activity grid: column header for the result of each MCP tool call (Ok, Refused or Error).

column_reason.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Activity grid: column header for the explanation recorded when an MCP tool call was refused or failed; empty for successful calls.

column_rows.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Activity grid: column header for the number of rows returned or affected by an MCP tool call.

column_sql.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Activity grid: column header for the SQL text the AI client sent, with sensitive literals redacted; keep the acronym SQL.

column_time.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Activity grid: first column header, holding the date and time each MCP tool call was logged.

column_tool.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Activity grid: column header for the name of the MCP tool an AI client invoked (for example a query or schema tool).

dialog_title.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog: title of the dialog, opened from Settings → MCP, that lists the local audit log of every tool call AI clients made through SQLLY’s MCP server.

export_csv_button.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Toolbar: button that opens a save dialog and writes the currently filtered activity rows to a CSV file; the ellipsis signals that a file chooser follows.

export_json_button.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Toolbar: button that opens a save dialog and writes the currently filtered activity rows to a JSON file; the ellipsis signals that a file chooser follows.

exported_csv.location: Workbench → Status bar: confirmation shown after the MCP Activity dialog’s Export CSV… button finishes writing the CSV file; {path} is the full path of the saved .csv file.

exported_json.location: Workbench → Status bar: confirmation shown after the MCP Activity dialog’s Export JSON… button finishes writing the JSON file; {path} is the full path of the saved .json file.

filter_all_connections.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Toolbar: first option of the connection filter dropdown (third dropdown); selecting it shows activity for every connection.

filter_all_outcomes.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Toolbar: first option of the outcome filter dropdown (second dropdown); selecting it shows successful, refused and failed calls together.

filter_all_tools.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Toolbar: first option of the tool filter dropdown (leftmost dropdown); selecting it shows calls to every MCP tool.

footer.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Footer: summary line under the grid; {filtered_count} is how many log records match the current filters, {total_count} is how many were loaded, and {path} is the folder holding the audit log files.

outcome_error.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog: outcome value, used both in the Outcome column and the outcome filter dropdown, for an MCP tool call that failed while running (a noun, not a dialog title).

outcome_ok.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog: outcome value, used both in the Outcome column and the outcome filter dropdown, for an MCP tool call that completed successfully; very short.

outcome_refused.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog: outcome value, used both in the Outcome column and the outcome filter dropdown, for an MCP tool call that SQLLY blocked, for example by a connection safety rule.

refresh_button.location: Settings → MCP → MCP Activity dialog → Toolbar: small button right of the three filter dropdowns that reloads the audit log from disk to pick up new MCP calls.

estimate_unavailable.location: Workbench → Status bar and Notification Center → MCP write proposal pre-flight: message shown when an AI client proposes a data-changing statement and SQLLY could neither count the affected rows nor summarise a query plan for it.

estimate_unavailable_reason.location: Workbench → Status bar and Notification Center → MCP write proposal pre-flight: message shown when the impact estimate for an AI-proposed write statement failed; {reason} is the database error or timeout explanation.

estimated_rows.location: Workbench → Status bar and Notification Center → MCP write proposal pre-flight: impact estimate shown before running an AI-proposed UPDATE or DELETE; {rows} is the number of rows its WHERE clause currently matches.

estimated_rows_with_plan.location: Workbench → Status bar and Notification Center → MCP write proposal pre-flight: impact estimate with plan for an AI-proposed UPDATE or DELETE; {rows} is the number of matching rows and {plan} is a one-line summary of the top query plan operator.

plan_rows.location: Workbench → Status bar and Notification Center → MCP write proposal pre-flight: one-line query plan summary inserted into the impact estimate; {node_type} is the top plan operator (e.g. a table scan) and {rows} is the planner’s estimated row count.

query_timeout.location: Workbench → Status bar and Notification Center → MCP write proposal pre-flight: reason text, inserted after “Estimate unavailable:”, used when the row count or plan query for an AI-proposed write took longer than 5 seconds and was abandoned; starts lowercase.

about.location: Application menu bar → SQLLY menu (macOS): first item; opens the About window with the version, license and acknowledgments.

check_updates.location: Application menu bar → SQLLY menu (macOS): item under About, shown in editions that update themselves, that checks the server for a newer SQLLY version.

preferences.location: Application menu bar → SQLLY menu (macOS): item that opens the Settings window; use the standard macOS name for the app preferences command.

quit.location: Application menu bar → SQLLY menu (macOS): last item; quits the SQLLY application; use the standard macOS name for the quit command.

services.location: Application menu bar → SQLLY menu (macOS): submenu holding the system Services provided by macOS; use the standard macOS name for this submenu.

title.location: Application menu bar → SQLLY application menu: title of the macOS application menu, the first menu next to the Apple menu; it is the product name, normally left untranslated.

unlock.location: Application menu bar → SQLLY menu (macOS): item under About, shown only in the Mac App Store edition, that opens the in-app purchase window to unlock the full version.

add_cursor_above.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Multi-cursor group: item that adds an extra text cursor on the line above in the SQL editor.

add_cursor_below.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Multi-cursor group: item that adds an extra text cursor on the line below in the SQL editor.

add_cursor_next_occurrence.value: Ajouter un curseur pour la prochaine occurrence
add_cursor_next_occurrence.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Multi-cursor group: item that adds a cursor at the next occurrence of the selected text or word in the SQL editor.

add_line_comment.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Comment group: item that comments out the current or selected lines in the SQL editor with “--”, even if already commented.

convert_delimited_list.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → List tools group: item that opens a dialog converting the selected comma-, tab- or line-separated text into another delimited or quoted list.

copy.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Clipboard group: standard item that copies the current selection to the clipboard.

cut.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Clipboard group: standard item that removes the current selection and places it on the clipboard.

find.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Search group: item that opens the find bar in the SQL editor to search the query text.

find_next.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Search group: item that jumps to the next match of the current search text in the SQL editor.

find_previous.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Search group: item that jumps to the previous match of the current search text in the SQL editor.

format_document.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu: item that reformats the entire SQL editor contents using the formatting settings (indentation, keyword case, line breaks).

insert_distinct_in_list.value: Insérer des valeurs distinctes sous forme de liste IN
insert_distinct_in_list.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → List tools group: item that queries the distinct values of the column under the cursor and inserts them as an IN (…) list.

move_beginning.value: Aller au début de la ligne
move_beginning.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Navigation group: item that moves the editor cursor to the start of the current line (first non-blank character, then column one).

move_end.value: Aller à la fin de la ligne
move_end.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Navigation group: item that moves the editor cursor to the end of the current line.

page_down.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Navigation group: item that moves the editor cursor down by one visible page of lines.

page_up.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Navigation group: item that moves the editor cursor up by one visible page of lines.

paste.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Clipboard group: standard item that inserts the clipboard contents at the cursor.

paste_in_list.value: Coller sous forme de liste IN
paste_in_list.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → List tools group: item that pastes clipboard lines (for example a copied spreadsheet column) into the SQL editor as a quoted IN (…) value list.

redo.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu: second item; standard command that reapplies the edit last undone.

remove_line_comment.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Comment group: item that removes the leading “--” comment marker from the current or selected lines in the SQL editor.

replace.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Search group: item that opens the find bar with the replace field, to substitute text in the SQL editor.

select_all.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Clipboard group: standard item that selects all text in the focused editor or field.

select_all_occurrences.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Multi-cursor group: item that places a cursor on every occurrence of the selected text or word in the SQL editor at once.

select_beginning.value: Sélectionner jusqu’au début de la ligne
select_beginning.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Navigation group: item that extends the selection from the cursor to the start of the current line.

select_end.value: Sélectionner jusqu’à la fin de la ligne
select_end.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Navigation group: item that extends the selection from the cursor to the end of the current line.

select_page_down.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Navigation group: item that extends the selection downward by one visible page of lines.

select_page_up.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Navigation group: item that extends the selection upward by one visible page of lines.

title.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu: title of the Edit menu, holding undo/redo, clipboard, find/replace, multi-cursor, list, formatting and comment commands; use the standard name of this menu.

toggle_line_comment.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Comment group: item that comments the current or selected lines with “--”, or uncomments them if they already are.

trigger_suggest.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Completion group: item that opens the IntelliSense completion list at the cursor in the SQL editor (tables, columns, keywords).

undo.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu: first item; standard command that reverts the last edit.

value_autocomplete.value: Saisie semi-automatique des valeurs de colonne
value_autocomplete.location: Application menu bar → Edit menu → Completion group: item that opens a completion popup listing actual distinct values from the database for the column at the cursor.

close.location: Application menu bar → File menu: last item on macOS (before Exit on Windows); closes the active query tab, asking to save unsaved changes.

exit.location: Application menu bar → File menu (Windows and Linux only): final item that quits the SQLLY application; use the standard Windows name for this command.

export_connections.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Open/Import group: item that opens a picker to choose saved connections and writes them to a connection file without passwords.

export_credentials.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Open/Import group: item that exports chosen saved connections to a file including their passwords in clear text.

import_connections.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Open/Import group: item that imports saved connections from a SQLLY connection file into the connection list.

import_other_tools.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Open/Import group: item that imports connection definitions from another database tool’s configuration file (for example DBeaver or DataGrip); a noun phrase meaning “from other tools”.

export_other_tools.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Open/Import group: submenu title whose items each save the chosen saved connections in another database tool's own connection-file format (pgAdmin, Azure Data Studio, DBeaver, DataGrip, DbGate, PostgreSQL service file).

export_other_tools_pgadmin.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Export for Other Tools submenu: item that saves PostgreSQL connections as a pgAdmin servers.json file; keep the product and file names unchanged.

export_other_tools_azure_data_studio.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Export for Other Tools submenu: item that saves connections as an Azure Data Studio / VS Code settings.json file; keep the product and file names unchanged.

export_other_tools_dbeaver.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Export for Other Tools submenu: item that saves connections as a DBeaver data-sources.json file; keep the product and file names unchanged.

export_other_tools_datagrip.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Export for Other Tools submenu: item that saves connections as a DataGrip / JetBrains dataSources.xml file; keep the product and file names unchanged.

export_other_tools_dbgate.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Export for Other Tools submenu: item that saves connections as a DbGate connection environment (.env) file; keep the product and file names unchanged.

export_other_tools_pg_service.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Export for Other Tools submenu: item that saves PostgreSQL connections as a PostgreSQL connection service file read by psql and other libpq tools; keep the file name unchanged.

manage_workspaces.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Workspace group: item that opens the workspace dialog to rename, delete or switch between saved workspaces.

new_query.location: Application menu bar → File menu: first item; opens a new empty SQL query tab in the editor.

new_window.location: Application menu bar → File menu: item that opens an additional SQLLY workbench window.

open_export.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Open/Import group: item that opens a file chooser to load a saved SQLLY export (.sqllyexport) file.

open_folder.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Open/Import group: item that chooses a folder and lists every .sql file inside it, recursively, in the project file picker.

open_project_file.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Open/Import group: item that opens SQLLY’s own project file picker (folder and project SQL modes with preview) instead of the system open dialog.

open_sql.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Open/Import group: first open item; shows the system file chooser to open a .sql script into a query tab (short form, listed just above Open SQL file).

open_sql_file.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Open/Import group: second open item, directly below Open SQL; also shows the system file chooser to load a .sql script into a query tab.

open_workspace.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Workspace group: item that opens the workspace dialog to choose a saved workspace (set of tabs and connections) to restore.

run_sql_file.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Open/Import group (desktop only): item that opens the Run SQL File dialog to execute a .sql script from disk against the current connection without loading it into the editor.

save_library.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Save group: item that saves the active query tab into the SQL Library folder as a reusable snippet.

save_results.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Save group: item that exports the current result grid to a file (CSV, Excel or other export formats).

save_sql.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Save group: item that saves the active query tab’s SQL text to its .sql file, prompting for a location the first time.

save_workspace_as.location: Application menu bar → File menu → Workspace group: item that saves the current tabs and connections as a new named workspace.

title.location: Application menu bar → File menu: title of the File menu, holding new, open, import/export, workspace, save and close commands; use the standard name of this menu.

about.location: Application menu bar → Help menu: menu item on every platform that opens SQLLY's version and credits, in a window on desktop or an in-app panel in the browser; last item below a separator on Windows and Linux, noun phrase as in “About SQLLY”.

app_store_edition.location: Application menu bar → Help menu: menu item shown only in the Mac App Store build that opens a dialog explaining the App Store edition and its purchase/limits; “edition” means product variant.

check_updates.location: Application menu bar → Help menu: menu item on Windows and Linux that checks whether a newer SQLLY version is available and reports the result in the status bar; imperative command.

formatting_directives.location: Application menu bar → Help menu: menu item that opens the reference window listing SQLLY formatting directives (special comments that control result-grid formatting) and their syntax.

open_source_licenses.location: Application menu bar → Help menu: menu item that opens a window listing every third-party open-source project SQLLY uses with the full text of its license.

privacy_policy.location: Application menu bar → Help menu: menu item that opens the SQLLY privacy policy web page in the default browser.

send_feedback.location: Application menu bar → Help menu: menu item that screenshots the current window and opens the feedback dialog where the user can annotate it and send a report to the SQLLY team; imperative command.

show_commands.location: Application menu bar → Help menu: menu item that opens the Command Palette listing every available command (same as View menu → Command palette); imperative command.

sqlly_help.location: Application menu bar → Help menu: first menu item, opens a help window generated from the live command list and keyboard shortcuts; “Sqlly” is the product name and stays untranslated.

tip_of_day.location: Application menu bar → Help menu: menu item that opens the Tip of the Day popup showing a short rotating tip about a SQLLY feature on demand.

title.location: Application menu bar → Help menu: title of the top-level Help menu, the last menu on the bar, holding help, feedback, licenses and About items; one short word.

ask_schema.location: Application menu bar → Query menu: menu item that opens the AI panel on its Ask tab to ask natural-language questions about the connected database’s schema.

cancel.location: Application menu bar → Query menu: last menu item, stops the query currently running in the active editor tab; imperative verb.

execute.location: Application menu bar → Query menu: first menu item, runs the SQL in the active editor tab (or the selection) and shows the results below, replacing previous results; imperative verb.

execute_new_result_tab.value: Exécuter dans un nouvel onglet de résultats
execute_new_result_tab.location: Application menu bar → Query menu: menu item that runs the active tab’s SQL but keeps earlier results, placing the new results in an additional result tab; command phrase.

explain_actual.value: Expliquer la requête (réel, exécute la requête)
explain_actual.location: Application menu bar → Query menu: menu item that runs the query and opens the actual execution plan viewer with real runtime statistics; contrast with “Explain estimated”.

explain_estimated.location: Application menu bar → Query menu: menu item that opens the estimated execution plan for the active query without running it; contrast with “Explain actual”.

format.location: Application menu bar → Query menu: menu item that reformats (pretty-prints) the SQL in the active editor tab using the formatting settings; imperative verb.

generate_sql.location: Application menu bar → Query menu: menu item that opens the AI panel on its Generate SQL tab, where a plain-language request is turned into a SQL query.

minify.location: Application menu bar → Query menu: menu item that compacts the SQL in the active editor tab onto as few lines as possible by removing extra whitespace; opposite of Format.

run_multiple.location: Application menu bar → Query menu: menu item that opens a dialog to run the active query against several saved connections at once and compare the results.

title.location: Application menu bar → Query menu: title of the top-level Query menu holding run, cancel, execution plan, AI, validate and format commands for the active editor tab.

toggle_ai.location: Application menu bar → Query menu: menu item that shows or hides the AI assistant side panel; “Toggle” means show if hidden, hide if shown.

validate.location: Application menu bar → Query menu: menu item that checks the active tab’s SQL for syntax and reference errors without running it and marks problems in the editor; imperative verb.

add_firewall_ip.value: Ajouter mon IP au pare-feu du serveur…
add_firewall_ip.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu: menu item that adds this computer’s public IP address as a firewall rule on the connected Azure SQL server so it can connect; “IP” is an IP address.

azure_connection.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu: menu item that opens the Azure SQL connection flow to sign in to Azure and pick a server and database to connect to.

chart_dashboard.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu: menu item that opens the Chart Dashboard window showing saved charts together on one board.

connect.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu: menu item shown in place of “Disconnect” when no connection is active; opens the connection dialog to connect to a database server; imperative verb.

connection_management.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu: menu item that opens the Connection Management dialog for adding, editing, organizing and deleting saved connections.

disconnect.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu: menu item shown in place of “Connect” while a connection is active; closes the current database connection; imperative verb.

go_to_object.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu: menu item (also in the View menu) that opens the quick-open search box to jump to a table, view or other database object by name.

import_clipboard.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu: menu item that opens the import wizard with copied clipboard data (e.g. cells from a spreadsheet) as the source to load into a table.

keyboard_shortcuts.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu: last menu item, opens Settings at the Keyboard Shortcuts page to view and change key bindings.

manage_entities.value: Gérer les clients, projets et environnements…
manage_entities.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu: menu item that opens the dialog for managing clients, projects and environments (named groups with colors and safety settings that connections belong to).

object_browser.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu: menu item that opens the Object Browser, a sortable inventory of the database’s tables, views, routines and triggers with details and batch scripts.

object_properties.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu: menu item that opens the properties editor for the connected server or selected object, the same dialog as the explorer’s context menu.

options.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu: menu item on Windows and Linux (labeled “Preferences” on macOS) that opens the Settings window; use the platform’s usual word for app options.

preferences.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu: menu item on macOS (labeled “Options” on Windows and Linux) that opens the Settings window; use the macOS-standard word for app preferences.

refresh_explorer.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu: first menu item, reloads the object explorer tree in the sidebar so newly created or dropped database objects appear; imperative command.

result_snapshots.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu: menu item that opens the Result Snapshots browser listing saved captures of result sets that reopen read-only without rerunning the query.

saved_charts.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu: menu item that opens the list of charts the user has saved from query results, to reopen, rename or delete them.

template_explorer.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu: menu item that opens the Template Explorer, a catalog of ready-made SQL script templates with fill-in parameters that insert into a new tab.

title.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu: title of the top-level Tools menu holding connection, Azure, object browser, snapshots, charts and settings commands.

actual_size.location: Application menu bar → View menu: menu item that resets the editor zoom level back to 100%, after Zoom in and Zoom out; standard “Actual Size” wording.

close_split.location: Application menu bar → View menu: menu item that removes the editor split and returns to a single editor pane; the other pane’s tab stays open in the tab bar.

command_palette.location: Application menu bar → View menu: first menu item, opens the Command Palette search box listing every command by name; product-style noun phrase.

go_to_object.location: Application menu bar → View menu: menu item (also in the Tools menu) that opens the quick-open box to jump to a database object or open tab by typing part of its name.

search_schema.location: Application menu bar → View menu: menu item that opens the AI panel on its Search tab to find tables and columns in the connected database by meaning or name.

show_sql_library.location: Application menu bar → View menu: menu item that shows the sidebar switched to the SQL Library of saved scripts; imperative “show”.

split_horizontal.location: Application menu bar → View menu: menu item that splits the editor into two panes stacked top and bottom, copying the active tab’s SQL into a new tab in the lower pane.

split_same_horizontal.location: Application menu bar → View menu: menu item that splits the editor top and bottom with both panes showing the same document (shared text, separate cursors and scrolling).

split_same_vertical.location: Application menu bar → View menu: menu item that splits the editor side by side with both panes showing the same document (shared text, separate cursors and scrolling).

split_vertical.location: Application menu bar → View menu: menu item that splits the editor into two side-by-side panes, copying the active tab’s SQL into a new tab in the right pane.

theme_dark.location: Application menu bar → View menu: theme menu item that switches the app to the dark color theme; reads like “Theme: Dark”.

theme_high_contrast.location: Application menu bar → View menu: theme menu item that switches the app to the high-contrast color theme for accessibility; reads like “Theme: High contrast”.

theme_light.location: Application menu bar → View menu: theme menu item that switches the app to the light color theme; reads like “Theme: Light”.

theme_system.location: Application menu bar → View menu: first theme menu item, makes the app follow the operating system’s light or dark appearance; reads like “Theme: System”.

title.location: Application menu bar → View menu: title of the top-level View menu holding panels, editor splits, zoom and color theme commands.

toggle_explorer.location: Application menu bar → View menu: menu item that shows or hides the left sidebar with the object explorer; “Toggle” means show if hidden, hide if shown.

toggle_intellisense_debug.value: Afficher ou masquer le panneau de débogage IntelliSense
toggle_intellisense_debug.location: Application menu bar → View menu: menu item that shows or hides a diagnostic panel with the SQL completion engine’s (IntelliSense) internal state; for troubleshooting.

toggle_log.value: Afficher ou masquer la console des journaux
toggle_log.location: Application menu bar → View menu: menu item that shows or hides the log console panel with the app’s activity log; “Toggle” means show if hidden, hide if shown.

toggle_results.value: Afficher ou masquer le volet des résultats
toggle_results.location: Application menu bar → View menu: menu item that shows or hides the results pane below the SQL editor; “Toggle” means show if hidden, hide if shown.

zoom_in.location: Application menu bar → View menu: menu item that increases the editor text zoom level one step; standard “Zoom In” wording.

zoom_out.location: Application menu bar → View menu: menu item that decreases the editor text zoom level one step; standard “Zoom Out” wording.

bring_all_front.location: Application menu bar → Window menu: macOS-only last menu item that brings all SQLLY windows in front of other apps; standard macOS “Bring All to Front” command.

close_tab.location: Application menu bar → Window menu: menu item that closes the active editor tab in the current window; imperative command.

maximize.location: Application menu bar → Window menu: Windows and Linux menu item (labeled “Zoom” on macOS) that maximizes the window or restores it from maximized size.

minimize.location: Application menu bar → Window menu: first menu item, minimizes the current SQLLY window to the Dock or taskbar; standard window command.

next_tab.location: Application menu bar → Window menu: menu item that switches to the editor tab to the right of the active one; imperative navigation command.

previous_tab.location: Application menu bar → Window menu: menu item that switches to the editor tab to the left of the active one; imperative navigation command.

reopen_closed_tab.location: Application menu bar → Window menu: menu item that reopens the most recently closed editor tab with its SQL; imperative command.

title.location: Application menu bar → Window menu: title of the top-level Window menu holding minimize, zoom/maximize, editor tab navigation and window arrangement commands.

zoom.location: Application menu bar → Window menu: macOS menu item (labeled “Maximize” elsewhere) that toggles the window between its standard and enlarged size; the macOS window “Zoom”, not text zoom.

clear_all.location: Workbench → Status bar → Notifications dialog: footer button that removes every notification from the list; disabled when the list is empty; imperative command.

reveal.location: Workbench → Status bar → Notifications dialog: small button on a notification row for a saved file (e.g. a finished export) that shows the file in Finder or Explorer; imperative verb.

title.location: Workbench → Status bar → Notifications dialog: title of the dialog opened by clicking the bell icon, listing recent query completions, failures, exports and updates.

empty.value: Rien pour l'instant — les terminaisons, échecs et mises à jour des requêtes de longue durée apparaissent ici.
empty.location: Workbench → Status bar → Notifications dialog: empty-state message in the list when no notifications have arrived yet, explaining what kinds of events will appear there.

item_timestamp.location: Workbench → Status bar → Notifications dialog: small dim header line above each notification message; {label} is the notification type (e.g. “Query completed”) and {time} is when it happened.

export_saved.location: Workbench → Status bar → Notifications dialog: notification type label for a finished file deliverable (result export, table data export or schema documentation); shown before the time.

query_completed.location: Workbench → Status bar → Notifications dialog: notification type label for a long-running query that finished successfully; shown before the time in the row header.

query_failed.location: Workbench → Status bar → Notifications dialog: notification type label for a long-running query that ended with an error; shown before the time in the row header.

update_available.location: Workbench → Status bar → Notifications dialog: notification type label for a notice that a newer SQLLY version can be installed; shown before the time in the row header.

system_toggle.location: Workbench → Status bar → Notifications dialog: checkbox label in the footer; when checked, SQLLY also posts operating-system notifications for these events while the app is in the background.

tooltip.location: Workbench → Status bar: tooltip on the bell icon button at the right of the status bar that opens the Notifications dialog; may show an unread count badge.

copy_license_button.location: Open Source Licenses → License block: button that copies that complete license text to the clipboard.

dependencies_heading.location: SQLLY → Open Source Licenses window: section heading above the grouped third-party dependency list.

header.location: SQLLY → Open Source Licenses window: main heading above the introduction and dependency catalog.

intro.value: SQLLY est construit sur le travail de la communauté open-source. Ci-dessous se trouvent tous les projets tiers dont SQLLY dépend, suivis du texte intégral de chaque licence sous laquelle ils sont distribués. Chaque licence est reproduite mot pour mot.
intro.location: SQLLY → Open Source Licenses window: introductory paragraph explaining the dependency list and verbatim license texts.

licenses_heading.location: SQLLY → Open Source Licenses window: section heading above the full third-party license texts.

used_by.location: Open Source Licenses → License block: line listing the comma-separated dependencies distributed under that license.

window_title.location: SQLLY → Open Source Licenses window: native title-bar caption for the third-party dependency and license viewer.

ambiguous_filter_help.value: Utilisez schema:, sch:, sproc:, proc:, ou p: pour les filtres de type SQL.
ambiguous_filter_help.location: Open Project File → Filter help: guidance shown for ambiguous s: prefix explaining unambiguous schema and procedure filters.

browser_demo_banner.value: À titre indicatif seulement — l'aperçu web ne peut pas lire les fichiers depuis votre ordinateur. Utilisez l'application de bureau pour ouvrir les fichiers du projet depuis le disque.
browser_demo_banner.location: Open Project File → Illustrative web preview: banner directing users to the desktop app for opening project files from disk.

browser_served_banner.value: SQLLY dans le navigateur ne peut pas lire les fichiers depuis votre ordinateur.
browser_served_banner.location: Open Project File → Browser preview: banner explaining that the browser-hosted application cannot read local files.

choose_folder_unavailable.value: Le choix d'un dossier de projet n'est pas disponible
choose_folder_unavailable.location: Open Project File → Browser preview: limitation status shown because browser-hosted SQLLY cannot choose a local project folder.

choose_root_button.location: Open Project File → Header: button that selects a different project root folder.

choose_root_prompt.value: Choisissez le dossier que SQLLY doit utiliser comme racine du projet.
choose_root_prompt.location: Open Project File → Choose Root: native folder-picker prompt explaining which folder to select.

copy_path_button.location: Open Project File → Preview actions: button that copies the selected file or object path to the clipboard.

create_file_failed.location: Open Project File → New SQL File: error status naming the file that could not be created.

create_file_unavailable.value: La création de fichiers n'est pas disponible
create_file_unavailable.location: Open Project File → Browser preview: limitation status shown because browser-hosted SQLLY cannot create local files.

data_model_chip.location: Open Project File → Result row: source chip identifying an object loaded from the connected data model rather than disk.

ddl_toggle.location: Open Project File → Header: toggle that includes or excludes data-model objects whose definitions can be opened.

dialog_title.location: SQLLY → Open Project File dialog: title for choosing a SQL file or data-model object to open.

filter_placeholder.value: Rechercher des fichiers ou utiliser v:, p:, f:, schéma :
filter_placeholder.location: Open Project File → Filter: placeholder describing free-text search and common object and schema filter prefixes.

folder_empty.location: Open Project File → Folder mode: empty-state title shown when the selected folder has no visible entries.

folder_empty_detail.value: Créer un fichier SQL ici ou naviguer vers un autre dossier.
folder_empty_detail.location: Open Project File → Folder mode: empty-state guidance for adding a SQL file or changing folders.

folder_mode.location: Open Project File → Mode selector: segment that browses one filesystem folder at a time.

folder_path.location: Open Project File → Header: current directory path shown while Folder mode is active.

folder_unavailable.location: Open Project File → Folder mode: empty-state title shown when the current folder cannot be read.

folder_unavailable_detail.value: SQLLY n'a pas pu lire {path}. Choisissez un autre dossier ou vérifiez les autorisations.
folder_unavailable_detail.location: Open Project File → Folder mode: empty-state detail naming the unreadable folder and suggesting recovery steps.

git_button.location: Open Project File → Footer: button that opens Git actions for the current project root.

git_tooltip.value: Statut Git, diff, et commit pour ce dossier de projet
git_tooltip.location: Open Project File → Footer → Git button: tooltip summarizing the available repository actions.

hidden_toggle.location: Open Project File → Header: toggle that includes or excludes hidden files and folders.

kind_function.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: object-kind chip or match reason for a function.

kind_index.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: object-kind chip or match reason for an index.

kind_sproc.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: object-kind chip or match reason for a stored procedure.

kind_table.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: object-kind chip or match reason for a table.

kind_trigger.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: object-kind chip or match reason for a trigger.

kind_type.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: object-kind chip or match reason for a user-defined type.

kind_unknown.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: object-kind chip shown when SQL metadata does not identify an object type.

kind_view.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: object-kind chip or match reason for a view.

load_full_button.location: Open Project File → Preview actions: button that reloads a truncated SQL preview without byte or line limits.

loading_files.location: Open Project File → List status: progress message shown while loading a newly selected folder.

match_chip.location: Open Project File → Result row: chip explaining which localized field or object type matched the active filter.

match_name.location: Open Project File → Result match chip: reason indicating that the file name matched the filter.

match_object.location: Open Project File → Result match chip: reason indicating that the SQL object name matched the filter.

match_path.location: Open Project File → Result match chip: reason indicating that the relative file path matched the filter.

match_schema.location: Open Project File → Result match chip: reason indicating that the schema name matched the filter.

multiple_objects_chip.location: Open Project File → Result row: metadata chip indicating that a SQL script contains multiple top-level objects.

new_file_button.location: Open Project File → Header: button that creates and opens a new SQL file.

no_matches.location: Open Project File → List empty state: title shown when the active filter excludes every scanned row.

no_matches_detail.value: Effacez le filtre ou supprimez le préfixe pour voir plus de fichiers.
no_matches_detail.location: Open Project File → List empty state: guidance for broadening a filter that has no matches.

open_button.location: Open Project File → Footer: primary button that opens the selected SQL file or data-model definition.

preview_folder_detail.value: Les dossiers ne génèrent pas d'aperçus SQL.
preview_folder_detail.location: Open Project File → Preview → Folder: explanation shown instead of SQL content for a folder selection.

preview_invalid_utf8.value: Aperçu indisponible : le fichier n'est pas valide en UTF-8.
preview_invalid_utf8.location: Open Project File → Preview: error detail shown when the selected SQL file is not valid UTF-8 text.

preview_missing_title.location: Open Project File → Preview: title shown when the selected SQL file disappeared before it could be loaded.

preview_model_detail.value: La définition est récupérée à partir de la base de données connectée lors de l'ouverture (génération DDL au style sp_helptext).
preview_model_detail.location: Open Project File → Preview → Data-model object: explanation that opening the object fetches its definition from the connected database.

preview_multiple_objects.value: objets multiples ; affichage du premier objet de niveau supérieur
preview_multiple_objects.location: Open Project File → Preview metadata: note that the script contains several objects and metadata describes only the first.

preview_no_selection.location: Open Project File → Preview: title shown when no file or data-model object is selected.

preview_select_file.value: Sélectionnez un fichier SQL pour l'apercevoir.
preview_select_file.location: Open Project File → Preview: guidance shown when there is no selection to preview.

preview_sql_only.value: L'aperçu est disponible uniquement pour les fichiers .sql.
preview_sql_only.location: Open Project File → Preview: explanation shown when the selected file does not have a .sql extension.

preview_truncated.location: Open Project File → Preview metadata: note that displayed SQL was limited by byte or line count.

preview_unreadable.value: Aperçu non disponible : le fichier n'a pas pu être lu.
preview_unreadable.location: Open Project File → Preview: error detail shown when the selected SQL file cannot be read.

project_empty_detail.value: Passer en mode Dossier, choisir une autre racine ou créer un fichier SQL.
project_empty_detail.location: Open Project File → Project SQL mode: empty-state guidance shown when no SQL files are found under the root.

project_empty_title.location: Open Project File → Project SQL mode: empty-state title naming the scanned project root.

project_mode.location: Open Project File → Mode selector: segment that recursively lists SQL files under the project root.

project_path.location: Open Project File → Header: current project-root path shown while Project SQL mode is active.

project_root_unavailable.location: Open Project File → Project SQL mode: empty-state title shown when the configured project root does not exist.

project_root_unavailable_detail.value: Choisissez une autre racine de projet pour utiliser le mode SQL du projet.
project_root_unavailable_detail.location: Open Project File → Project SQL mode: empty-state guidance for recovering from a missing project root.

refreshing_files.location: Open Project File → List status: progress message shown after changing hidden-file visibility.

reveal_button.location: Open Project File → Preview actions: button that reveals the selected file in the operating system file manager.

scan_limit.value: Limite de fichiers scannés atteinte pour le projet ; réduisez la racine ou filtrez les résultats.
scan_limit.location: Open Project File → Project SQL scan summary: warning that recursive scanning stopped at its file limit and guidance for narrowing results.

scanning_files.location: Open Project File → List status: progress message shown after changing the file-browsing mode.

scanning_indicator.location: Open Project File → Header: compact activity indicator shown during a filesystem scan.

scanning_project.location: Open Project File → List status: progress message shown while recursively scanning the project root.

skipped_folder_plural.location: Open Project File → Project SQL scan summary: warning that multiple unreadable folders were skipped.

skipped_folder_singular.location: Open Project File → Project SQL scan summary: warning that one unreadable folder was skipped.

skipped_symlink_plural.value: Liens symboliques {count} en dehors de la racine du projet ignorés.
skipped_symlink_plural.location: Open Project File → Project SQL scan summary: warning that multiple symbolic links escaping the project root were skipped.

skipped_symlink_singular.value: Lien symbolique {count} en dehors de la racine du projet ignoré.
skipped_symlink_singular.location: Open Project File → Project SQL scan summary: warning that one symbolic link escaping the project root was skipped.

source_indexed.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: confidence chip indicating that scanned metadata also exists in the live schema catalog.

source_scan_only.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: confidence chip for trigger and index metadata available only from SQL text scanning.

source_scanned.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: confidence chip indicating that metadata was inferred from SQL file text.

source_unknown.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: confidence chip shown when no object metadata source is known.

unknown_schema_chip.location: Open Project File → Result metadata: schema chip shown when no schema could be inferred for the selected object.

up_button.location: Open Project File → Header: button that navigates to the parent folder without leaving the project boundary.

browser_unavailable.value: Les résumés IA ne sont pas disponibles
browser_unavailable.location: Browser version → Query editor → AI summary: phrase naming the unavailable feature, inserted into a “… is not available in the browser” message when an AI query summary is requested.

generate_http_status.location: Query editor → AI summary: error detail when the local AI runtime rejects a summary-generation request; {status} is the HTTP status code and reason, e.g. “500 Internal Server Error”.

http_failed.location: Query editor → AI summary and Settings → AI: error message wrapping a network failure talking to the local AI runtime; {message} is the underlying error text.

invalid_request.location: Query editor → AI summary: short internal error used when a summary is requested with empty SQL or no AI model selected; lowercase fragment.

invalid_response.location: Query editor → AI summary: short error used when the local AI runtime replies with something that cannot be read as a summary; lowercase fragment.

long_pending.value: Le résumé long n'a pas encore été généré
long_pending.location: Tab switcher (Ctrl+Tab) → Tab summary placeholder: placeholder shown under a tab’s name when no AI summary of its query has been generated yet.

models_http_status.location: Settings → AI → On device: error detail when checking the local AI runtime’s installed models fails; {status} is the HTTP status code and reason, e.g. “404 Not Found”.

runtime_unreachable_browser.value: le runtime IA local n'est pas accessible
runtime_unreachable_browser.location: Browser version → Settings → AI → On device: phrase inserted into a “… is not available in the browser” message after clicking the check-runtime button; lowercase fragment.

short_pending.value: Le résumé court n'a pas encore été généré
short_pending.location: Query editor → AI summary: placeholder meaning the one-line short summary of the tab’s query has not been generated yet; companion of the long-summary placeholder.

interval_off.location: Results → Status bar → Auto-refresh dropdown: button label and first menu option when the query is not re-run automatically; shown only for SELECT-only queries.

interval_one_minute.location: Results → Status bar → Auto-refresh dropdown: button label and menu option for re-running the query every minute; “1m” is an abbreviation of one minute, keep short.

interval_seconds.location: Results → Status bar → Auto-refresh dropdown: button label and menu option for re-running the query on a timer; {seconds} is 5, 10 or 30; “s” abbreviates seconds.

accept_inferred_join_button.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Joins: small button on a dimmed, suggested join row inferred from column names (no foreign key); adds that suggested join to the query. Short verb.

add_filter_button.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Where: button below the filter rows that adds a new WHERE condition, prefilled with the first available column.

add_join_button.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Joins: button below the join list that opens column pickers for defining a join by hand between two tables on the canvas.

add_order_button.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Order by: button that adds an ORDER BY row for the first selected column, ascending by default.

alias_placeholder.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Columns: placeholder in the optional input beside each selected column where the user types a column alias (AS name). Single lowercase word.

and_placeholder.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Where: placeholder in the second value input of a BETWEEN-style condition, i.e. the upper bound after “and”. Single lowercase word.

cancel_join_button.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Joins → manual join editor: button beside “Add” that discards the join being defined and closes the column pickers.

columns_caption.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel: small dim section heading above the DISTINCT switch and the list of selected output columns.

confirm_join_button.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Joins → manual join editor: button under the from/to column pickers that adds the defined inner join to the query. Short verb.

dialog_title.location: Query Builder dialog → Title bar: title of the visual query builder window, opened from the Tools menu, the command palette, or a table's context menu in the object explorer.

error_disconnected_table.value: {alias} n'est pas joint à la première table
error_disconnected_table.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Preview: message shown in place of the SQL preview when a table on the canvas has no join path to the first table; {alias} is that table's alias.

error_group_by.value: Ajouter chaque colonne de la liste de sélection non agrégée à GROUP BY
error_group_by.location: Query → Query Builder → Validation: error shown when aggregates are selected without grouping every non-aggregate select-list column.

error_no_columns.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Preview: message shown in place of the SQL preview when tables are added but no output column is ticked yet; Insert and Run stay disabled.

error_no_tables.value: Ajouter une table pour commencer à construire une requête
error_no_tables.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Preview: message shown in place of the SQL preview while the canvas is empty, telling the user to pick a table from the list on the left.

filter_tables_placeholder.location: Query Builder dialog → Table list (left column): placeholder in the search box above the list of database tables; typing narrows the list by name.

group_by_caption.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel: small dim section heading above the GROUP BY controls (SQL clause name).

inferred_join_label.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Joins: dim tag at the end of a join row that was guessed from column names rather than a foreign key; {percent} is the model's confidence (0–100).

insert_button.location: Query Builder dialog → footer: button that pastes the formatted SQL from the preview into the active editor tab and closes the dialog; disabled while the query is incomplete.

joins_caption.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel: small dim section heading at the top of the panel, above the list of joins between tables.

limit_caption.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel: small dim section heading above the row-limit input (caps how many rows the generated query returns).

limit_placeholder.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Limit: placeholder in the numeric input where the user types the maximum number of rows to return.

loading_tables.location: Query Builder dialog → Table list (left column): status line with a spinner under the filter box while the connected database's tables are still being loaded and the list is empty; tells the user the dialog is working, not frozen.

no_matching_tables.value: Aucune table ne correspond au filtre
no_matching_tables.location: Query Builder dialog → Table list (left column): status line under the filter box when the typed filter matches no table or view name.

no_tables.value: Aucune table dans cette base de données
no_tables.location: Query Builder dialog → Table list (left column): status line under the filter box when the connected database finished loading and has no tables or views.

order_by_caption.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel: small dim section heading above the ORDER BY rows and the “Add order” button (SQL clause name).

preview_caption.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel: small dim section heading above the live, formatted SQL preview box at the bottom of the panel.

refreshing_tables.value: Actualisation de la liste des tables…
refreshing_tables.location: Query Builder dialog → Table list (left column): status line with a spinner under the filter box while the table list (shown from cache) is being refreshed from the server in the background.

run_button.location: Query Builder dialog → footer: primary button that sends the generated SQL to an editor tab and executes it; disabled while the query is incomplete. Imperative verb.

value_placeholder.location: Query Builder dialog → Clauses panel → Where: placeholder in the first value input of a filter condition, where the user types the value to compare the column against. Single lowercase word.

where_caption.location: Query → Query Builder → Filters: caption above the WHERE condition rows.

baseline_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: button showing which earlier capture is the baseline; clicking cycles to the next capture. {capture} is a label like “Capture 2 · Estimated plan”.

baseline_required.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: warning shown instead of results when no baseline capture is available to compare from.

capture_label.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: name of one captured plan inside the Baseline/Comparison buttons; {sequence} is the capture number, {kind} is “Estimated plan” or “Actual plan”.

capture_not_retained.value: Cette capture contient {node_count} opérateurs et n'a pas été retenue pour la comparaison (limite : {limit}).
capture_not_retained.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Findings view: warning at the bottom of the pane when a very large plan is shown but not kept for later comparison; {node_count} is its operator count, {limit} the maximum.

capture_unavailable.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: fallback text inside the Baseline or Comparison button when the selected capture no longer exists. Single word.

capturing_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: disabled label of the Re-capture button while a new plan capture is running. Short progress word.

capturing_status.location: Results → Execution Plan pane: centered progress message in the pane body while a plan is being captured; {kind} is the lowercase plan type, “estimated plan” or “actual plan”.

compare_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: button shown once two or more plans were captured; switches the pane to a side-by-side comparison of two captures.

comparison_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: button showing which capture is compared against the baseline; clicking cycles to the next capture. {capture} is a label like “Capture 3 · Actual plan”.

comparison_delta_counts.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: dim second summary line counting changed operators; each placeholder is the number of operators that regressed, improved, were added, or were removed.

comparison_required.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: warning shown instead of results when no capture is selected to compare against the baseline.

comparison_summary.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: first summary line; {cost_delta} is the signed total-cost change, then operator and warning counts before (baseline) and after (comparison) with an arrow.

copy_finding_sql_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Findings view → finding row: small button that copies the finding's suggested fix SQL to the clipboard; shown only for findings that include SQL.

delta_actual_baseline.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: detail fragment when only the baseline plan has actual row counts; {before} is that count. Lowercase fragment joined with “·”.

delta_actual_change.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: detail fragment showing actual (measured) rows before → after; {before} baseline, {after} comparison. Lowercase fragment.

delta_actual_comparison.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: detail fragment when only the comparison plan has actual row counts; {after} is that count. Lowercase fragment.

delta_actual_unavailable.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: detail fragment when neither plan has actual row counts (e.g. both are estimated plans). Lowercase fragment.

delta_cost_baseline.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: cost fragment when the operator exists only in the baseline plan; {before} is its estimated cost. Lowercase fragment.

delta_cost_change.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: cost fragment showing estimated cost before → after with the signed difference {delta} in parentheses. Lowercase fragment.

delta_cost_comparison.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: cost fragment when the operator exists only in the comparison plan; {after} is its estimated cost. Lowercase fragment.

delta_cost_unavailable.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: cost fragment when neither plan reports a cost for the operator. Lowercase fragment.

delta_detail.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: dim detail line joining four fragments with “·”: cost, estimated rows, actual rows and warnings change. Keep the order and separators.

delta_estimated_baseline.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: fragment when only the baseline plan has an estimated row count; {before} is that estimate. Lowercase fragment.

delta_estimated_change.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: fragment showing the optimizer's estimated rows before → after; {before} baseline, {after} comparison. Lowercase fragment.

delta_estimated_comparison.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: fragment when only the comparison plan has an estimated row count; {after} is that estimate. Lowercase fragment.

delta_estimated_unavailable.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: fragment when neither plan has an estimated row count for the operator. Lowercase fragment.

delta_kind_added.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: colored status tag in the narrow left column for an operator that appears only in the comparison plan. Single word.

delta_kind_improved.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: green status tag in the narrow left column for an operator whose cost or rows got better. Single word.

delta_kind_regressed.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: red status tag in the narrow left column for an operator that got more expensive or worse. Single word.

delta_kind_removed.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: colored status tag in the narrow left column for an operator present in the baseline but gone from the comparison plan. Single word.

delta_statement.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: first line naming where the change is; {number} is the statement number in the batch, {operator} the plan operator name.

delta_warnings_changed.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: warnings fragment; {count} is the signed change in warning count, e.g. +2 or -1. Lowercase fragment.

delta_warnings_unchanged.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view → operator change row: warnings fragment when the operator has the same number of warnings in both plans. Lowercase fragment.

diagram_actual_subtitle.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Diagram view: second line inside an operator box of an actual plan; {cost_percent} is its share of total cost, then estimated rows → actual rows. Very short space.

diagram_estimated_subtitle.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Diagram view: second line inside an operator box of an estimated plan; {cost_percent} is its share of total cost, {estimated_rows} the estimated row count. Very short space.

diagram_help.value: défilez pour panoramique · cliquez sur un opérateur pour les détails
diagram_help.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Diagram view: small dim hint line above the plan diagram explaining that scrolling pans the canvas and clicking an operator box shows its details. Lowercase, “·”-separated.

different_query_context.value: Ces captures appartiennent à des textes de requête différents et ne peuvent pas être alignées en toute sécurité
different_query_context.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: warning shown instead of a comparison when the two chosen captures came from different SQL text, so operators cannot be matched up.

distinct_captures_required.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: warning shown when the Baseline and Comparison buttons point at the same capture; the user must pick two different ones.

empty_all_modes.value: Expliquez la requête actuelle (bouton Expliquer ou ⌘L) pour voir son plan ici.
empty_all_modes.location: Results → Execution Plan pane: empty-state guidance in the pane before any plan is captured, on engines that support both plan types; names the toolbar Explain button and its ⌘L shortcut.

empty_estimated_only.value: Expliquez la requête (Estimé, sans exécution) depuis le menu Requête ou la palette de commandes pour voir le plan de cette requête ici.
empty_estimated_only.location: Results → Execution Plan pane: empty-state guidance before any plan is captured, on engines that only support estimated plans; names the Query menu command “Explain Query (Estimated, No Execution)” and the command palette.

findings_count.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Findings view: dim section heading above the list of detected plan problems; {count} is how many findings this statement has.

findings_empty_plan.value: Le plan ne contenait aucune instruction.
findings_empty_plan.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Findings view: message filling the pane body when the captured plan has no statements to show findings for.

findings_operators_summary.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Findings view: dim section heading below the findings, above the operator list sorted by cost; {count} is the operator count, {total_cost} the statement's total cost.

kind_actual.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: dim label at the left of the header (also used inside capture names) when the plan came from actually running the query, with real row counts.

kind_estimated.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: dim label at the left of the header (also used inside capture names) when the plan is the optimizer's estimate, captured without running the query.

mode_diagram.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: view-switch button that shows the plan as a graphical diagram of operator boxes. Single noun.

mode_findings.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: view-switch button (the default) that shows ranked plan problems with suggested fixes, followed by operators by cost. Single noun.

mode_tree.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: view-switch button that shows the plan as an indented, collapsible operator tree. Single noun.

no_findings.value: Ce plan semble correct. Aucune anomalie détectée.
no_findings.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Findings view: reassuring message in place of the findings list when the analysis found no problems in this statement's plan.

no_operator_changes.value: Aucun changement d'opérateur matériel n'a été détecté.
no_operator_changes.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Comparison view: message in place of the operator change list when the two captures differ in no meaningful way per operator.

no_warnings.location: Execution plan text report → Warnings value: value used after “Warnings:” in the plan summary and in each operator's property block when there are no warnings. Single lowercase word.

node_properties.location: Execution plan text report → Operator property block: multi-line property block for one operator, one “label: value” per line; node id, physical and logical operation, estimated cost and its percent, estimated and actual rows, warnings.

not_available.location: Execution plan text report → operator property block: value after “Actual rows:” when the plan is estimated and has no measured row count. Very short abbreviation.

open_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: button that opens a file picker to load a saved execution plan file from disk into the pane.

open_finding_tab_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Findings view → finding row: small button beside “Copy SQL” that opens the finding's suggested fix SQL in a new editor tab.

output_heading.location: Execution plan text report → operator property block: heading line “Output” placed after a blank line, followed by a bulleted list of the operator's output columns.

paste_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: button that loads an execution plan (XML or JSON) from the clipboard into the pane.

recapture_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: button that captures the same kind of plan (estimated or actual) again for the current query; disabled with a tooltip when the engine can't.

select_operator.value: Sélectionnez un opérateur pour inspecter les propriétés.
select_operator.location: Execution plan text report → operator properties area: placeholder shown when no operator is selected, inviting the user to pick one to see its properties.

show_plan_button.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header: label of the Compare toggle while the comparison view is open; clicking returns to the normal single-plan view.

statement_fallback.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header → statement switcher: generic word used in a statement tab in place of the statement type when the plan does not name one.

statement_tab.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → header → statement switcher: tab for one statement of a multi-statement batch; {number} is its position, {statement_type} its kind (e.g. SELECT).

summary.location: Execution plan text report → Plan summary: multi-line plan summary at the top: statement text, type, total subtree cost, estimated rows, operator count, warnings, then a hint to select an operator box for details.

tree_empty.value: Le plan ne contenait aucune instruction.
tree_empty.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Tree view: message filling the pane body when the captured plan has no statements to build an operator tree from.

tree_operators_summary.location: Results → Execution Plan pane → Tree view: dim heading line above the operator tree; {count} is the number of operators, {total_cost} the statement's total subtree cost.

disconnected.value: Connectez-vous pour définir les options Explain
disconnected.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover (chevron beside the Explain button): message filling the popover when no connection is active, so plan options can't be set.

flag_analyze.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags: checkbox label for PostgreSQL/MySQL EXPLAIN ANALYZE; warns that the statement is actually executed to get real timings.

flag_buffers.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags (PostgreSQL): checkbox label for the BUFFERS option, adding shared/local buffer usage to the plan. Usually left as the technical term.

flag_costs.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags (PostgreSQL): checkbox label for the COSTS option, showing the optimizer's estimated startup and total cost per operator.

flag_generic_plan.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags (PostgreSQL 16+): checkbox label for the GENERIC_PLAN option, planning a parameterized query without specific parameter values.

flag_memory.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags (PostgreSQL 17+): checkbox label for the MEMORY option, reporting the planner's memory use.

flag_settings.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags (PostgreSQL 12+): checkbox label for the SETTINGS option, listing non-default planner configuration settings in the plan (not the app's settings).

flag_summary.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags (PostgreSQL): checkbox label for the SUMMARY option, adding planning and execution time totals after the plan.

flag_timing.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags (PostgreSQL): checkbox label for the TIMING option, recording actual time per operator when Analyze is on.

flag_unknown.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags: generic fallback checkbox label for an EXPLAIN option the app has no name for. Single noun.

flag_verbose.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags (PostgreSQL): checkbox label for the VERBOSE option, adding output column lists and schema-qualified names to the plan.

flag_wal.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → flags (PostgreSQL 13+): checkbox label for the WAL option, reporting write-ahead-log records generated. Acronym; usually kept as is.

preset_actual.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → preset buttons: button that captures an actual plan by running the query with the selected options. Short adjective; sits beside “Estimated” and “Profile”.

preset_estimated.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → preset buttons: button that captures an estimated plan without executing the query. Short adjective; sits beside “Actual” and “Profile”.

preset_profile.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover → preset buttons: button that runs and profiles the query to capture an actual plan, allowed only for read-only SELECT statements.

reset_defaults_button.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover: small text button at the bottom of the popover that restores every EXPLAIN option checkbox to its default state.

version_known.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover: dim line at the top of the popover naming the connected server; {product} is the engine (e.g. PostgreSQL), {major}.{minor} its version, which decides available flags.

version_probing.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover: dim line at the top of the popover while the app is still asking the server for its version, before flag availability is known.

version_unknown.location: Query toolbar → Explain options popover: dim line at the top of the popover when the server version could not be determined; flags assume a default version.

invalid_pins_file.value: Fichier de fragments épinglés non valide : {error}
invalid_pins_file.location: Query History dialog → Pinned snippets → Import: error in the status bar when the chosen file is not valid pinned-snippets JSON; {error} is the parser's technical reason.

age_days.location: Query History dialog → Entry list → Row detail line: relative age of an entry run 1–6 days ago, abbreviated (“d” = days); {count} is the number of days. Must stay very short; older entries show a plain date.

age_hours.location: Query History dialog → Entry list → Row detail line: relative age of an entry run 1–23 hours ago, abbreviated (“h” = hours); {count} is the number of hours. Must stay very short, sits among other “·”-separated details.

age_just_now.location: Query History dialog → Entry list → Row detail line: relative age shown for an entry run less than a minute ago, between the server/database and the outcome. Lowercase fragment, very short.

age_minutes.location: Query History dialog → Entry list → Row detail line: relative age of an entry run 1–59 minutes ago, abbreviated (“m” = minutes); {count} is the number of minutes. Must stay very short.

analyze_button.location: Query History dialog → Toolbar: button that sends the selected history entry (SQL, timing, outcome) to the AI panel for analysis and closes the dialog; disabled when nothing is selected.

analyze_recent_button.value: Analyser les 5 derniers visibles avec l’IA
analyze_recent_button.location: Query History dialog → Toolbar: button that sends the first five entries currently visible in the Recent section (after filtering) to the AI panel as one analysis request, then closes the dialog.

analyze_requires_selection.value: Sélectionnez d’abord une entrée de l’historique
analyze_requires_selection.location: Workbench → Status bar: info message shown when “Analyze with AI” in the Query History dialog is triggered with no history entry selected, asking the user to pick an entry first.

copy_rollback_button.location: Query History dialog → Toolbar: button that copies the rollback (undo) SQL recorded for the selected data-changing entry to the clipboard; enabled only when the entry has rollback SQL.

description_label.location: Query History dialog → Pinned snippet details: label in front of the free-text description input, shown only when the selected entry is pinned.

description_placeholder.location: Query History dialog → Pinned snippet details: placeholder in the description input for a selected pinned entry, inviting an optional note on what the query is for.

dialog_title.location: Query History dialog → Title bar: title of the modal dialog that lists previously run statements and pinned snippets, opened from the Query History command.

empty_history.value: Pas encore d’historique de requêtes — les instructions que vous exécutez sont enregistrées ici.
empty_history.location: Query History dialog → Entry list: empty-state message shown when no statements have ever been logged and nothing is pinned, explaining that statements you run will appear here.

empty_search.value: Aucune entrée ne correspond à la recherche.
